text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday.
- Ruling party MP Vladimir Seks proposes a new law to govern the property, income of state officials and their position on management and supervisory boards of Croatian companies.
- Many Croats may be disappointed by Austria's decision to impose tolls on its highways.
- A proposed law on long-term mortgages at interest rates marginally above inflation are expected to ease the purchase of vital housing.
- Stock market: Share prices on the decline again.
- While Croatian-built ships are receiving international prizes for quality, shipbuilders still piling-up losses.
- UN spokesperson in Belgrade, Susan Manuel on Serb families trickling out of the Croatian Danube region: We are not sure of the origins of those leaving.
- Trial of the 39 Serb paramilitaries, 27 of them in absentia, to commence in Zadar today.
- Is a new train strike on the horizon?
- Tudjman receives the health minister Andrija Hebrang and discusses with him the establishment of a medical team that will be monitoring his health. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
